name: Parallel octave-down bass for a thin ambient stereo take: duplicate the mix, pitch it down an octave at the same tempo, low-pass it at ~100 Hz (12 dB/oct), high-pass the original at the same point (24 dB/oct), squash the copy with a limiter and blend it in quietly, checking phase correlation
goal: Add weight to a thin one-take ambient/modular stereo recording (or a bounced pad/drone stem) without writing a new bass part: derive a sub layer by pitching a copy of the mix down one octave, crossover it against the original at about 100 Hz, remove its dynamics and tuck it underneath. Delta vs our bass-design variants: a sub generated from the existing material by octave transposition plus a complementary crossover, for when there are no multitracks.

source.title: Fix a Thin Mix: Easy Parallel Bass Trick for Ambient Music

prerequisites: DAW with pitch shifting/warping that keeps tempo
EQ/filters, a limiter, a spectrum analyzer and a phase-correlation meter

inputs.name: stereo_mix
inputs.description: Finished stereo take or stem whose low end rolls off steeply around 100 Hz

outputs.name: parallel_sub
outputs.description: Octave-down, low-passed, flattened copy blended under the original

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Octave shift is a fixed -12 semitone transposition; no pitch modulation.
The added layer supports the track; keep it quiet so it does not take over.
Crossover the two paths at the same frequency to avoid doubled frequencies and phase problems.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Analyse the mix: find where the low end rolls off (e.g. steeply below ~100 Hz).
Duplicate the track and pitch the copy down one octave while keeping the playback speed (warp/time-stretch). Energy at 100 Hz now appears at 50 Hz.
steps.expect: Octave-down copy in time with the original

steps.action: Turn the copy well down, then low-pass it gently (12 dB/oct) at about the original's roll-off (~100 Hz).
High-pass the original (24 dB/oct) at the same point so the two paths do not overlap.
Check a phase-correlation meter around 100 Hz; adjust the crossover if correlation drops.
steps.expect: No phase problems at the crossover

steps.action: Limit the copy aggressively (several dB of gain reduction, e.g. ~6-7 dB) so its dynamics are flattened, then set its level low and A/B on and off.
steps.expect: Steady, quiet sub support; mix feels heavier, not boomy

verification: Sub band (~40-80 Hz) shows new, steady energy after blending.
Correlation stays positive around the crossover.
Bypassing the copy makes the mix sound noticeably thinner, but enabling it does not mask the original.
